terms.comment: The prose word for a sheer face of rock, Caesar’s and Livy’s.

terms.gloss: a jutting rock or cliff, especially at sea
terms.comment: A rock or ledge standing out from the sea, on which ships are wrecked; mostly poetic, not in Cicero except figuratively (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: pendentem summā capream dē rūpe vidēbis: cāsūram spērēs; dēspicit illa canēs
phrases.english: you’ll see the wild goat hanging from the top of a cliff; you’d expect it to fall — it looks down on the dogs

sources: Lewis & Short: rupes · Lewis & Short: scopulus
